title: Celestia migration discovery - OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Discovery call to understand Celestia's interest in moving inference from OpenAI/hosted to Redwood Dedicated or Private. Key concerns: eval parity, vLLM/TGI compatibility, latency targets, data residency/SOC2/KMS, and benchmarking. Agreed next steps: share pricing + config doc, run a 1-week benchmark with sample workloads, and schedule a technical deep-dive with infra team.
next_steps: Samir to send Dedicated pricing and example configs (by 2026-09-17)
Jenna to share benchmark guide and request for sample prompts + dataset (by 2026-09-16)
Schedule performance deep dive with Celestia SREs (target week of 2026-09-21)
Customer to confirm data residency requirements and decision timeline (by 2026-09-24)
action_items: Samir: Email pricing + case study links by 2026-09-17
Jenna: Share benchmark spreadsheet and runbook by 2026-09-16
Maya: Provide sample eval set (500 prompts) and throughput target by 2026-09-17
Jonas: Confirm whether private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is needed for compliance by 2026-09-24
header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:38 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Liu (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CTO, Celestia), Luca Moretti (ML Engineer, Celestia), Priya Nair (Product), Jonas (SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE. quick intros?
[00:05] Maya: Hi this is Maya, CTO at Celestia Analytics, we run an insights platform for retail.
[00:10] Luca: Luca here, ML eng, primary owner of model infra.
[00:13] Priya: Priya, product.
[00:15] Jenna: Jenna, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:18] Jonas: Jonas on infra/SRE.
[00:22] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda: understand your current stack, pain points, and timeline for migration from OpenAI or any hosted provider to our Dedicated/Private offering. Jenna will jump into some technical Qs after.
[00:34] Maya: Cool, high level: we've been on OpenAI for the last 18 months. API for chat + embeddings. Costs have ballooned as usage scaled; also we want predictability and tighter data controls.
[00:46] Luca: Also experimenting with vLLM self-hosted for some batch jobs, and we tried TGI for faster iteration. But production parity is inconsistent — sometimes outputs differ from OpenAI and causes QA failures.
[01:00] Jenna: Got it. When you say parity, is that eval metrics drifting or exact response differences?
[01:06] Luca: Both. On our eval sets, Rouge/F1 dropped ~3-5% when running locally on vLLM quantized. And there are tokenization/stop-sequence differences.
[01:16] Priya: For the product team, we need consistent UX, so even small changes that change prompts meaningfully are an issue.
[01:23] Samir: Totally. A lot of customers see that. Our Dedicated environment aims to give you stable model variants and the ability to pin versions; we also do kernel selection and quantization profiles to preserve quality.
[01:34] Maya: Important for us: do you guarantee eval parity with OpenAI models? Or at least a way to measure and prevent regressions?
[01:41] Jenna: We don't claim 1:1 parity with OpenAI vendor models; what we do is provide a runbook for model onboarding, run benchmark comparisons, and automated quality monitors tied to your eval set. We can run side-by-side inference during a canary and flag regressions.
[01:55] Luca: How do you run benchmarks? We have long-context chat at 2-3k tokens and embeddings batches of 100k per day.
[02:04] Jenna: We have a benchmark harness — we'll share the spreadsheet and runbook. For Dedicated we can spin up mirrored environments and run identical workloads; we support batching, KV cache reuse, and you can test quantized variants.
[02:17] Maya: latency is a big metric. For chat our p95 should be under 300ms for 512 token exchanges. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[02:26] Jenna: On appropriately sized GPU pools and model choices, p95 under 300ms is in scope for small to medium sequence lengths. For larger seqs you'll see higher latency. We can show concrete numbers once we know model + instance type.
[02:37] Jonas: Are you providing autoscale and burst capacity? We have usage spikes during campaigns.
[02:42] Samir: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst options; we can set capacity buffers and fallbacks to hosted variants if needed.
[02:50] Priya: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — what's the posture for Private vs Dedicated?
[02:58] Jenna: Dedicated supports VPC peering, customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and detailed audit logs. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you more control — e.g., no cross-tenant metadata, on-prem image options. We'll send our security pack with SOC2/ISO docs.
[03:14] Luca: On the compatibility front: we use open-source stacks — vLLM + TGI — for a lot of workloads. How much effort is it to move models into Redwood?
[03:22] Jenna: We have a model onboarding guide. If you're using HF-compatible weights and standard architectures, it's usually straightforward. For custom TGI/vLLM forks we may need to validate runtime flags and tokenizer behavior. We can run a conversion step and validate on your eval set.
[03:36] Maya: Example: we have a finetuned Llama-2 variant with LoRA. Will that run?
[03:41] Jenna: In most cases yes. We'll need the exact weights and tokenizer, and we run a small staging inference to vet outputs. LoRA and PEFT variants are commonly supported.
[03:50] Luca: Cost — we're looking to reduce per-token cost compared to OpenAI. Any ballpark?
[03:55] Samir: Typically customers see 2-5x unit cost improvement moving to Dedicated depending on utilization and batching. Our Optimize toolkit gives concrete batching and quantization guidance to push unit cost down.
[04:08] Maya: Good. Timeline: we want a pilot in Q4, production by end of Q1. Is that doable?
[04:14] Samir: Yes, that's a common timeline. Pilot/POC usually 2-4 weeks for bench + quality eval, then Dedicated provisioning and rollout.
[04:22] Jonas: Any outages or fallbacks? We want graceful degradation — don't want calls to fail in traffic spikes.
[04:28] Jenna: We support smart routing and fallback to hosted variants or smaller models. Also canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies.
[04:36] Priya: Who is the support contact during pilot? We need SE hours for setup and troubleshooting.
[04:41] Samir: We'll include SE support in the pilot bundle; Jenna will be primary contact.
[04:46] Maya: Ok, concrete asks: 1) pricing and example Dedicated config 2) benchmark runbook + spreadsheet 3) a small bench (we'll provide prompts) 4) security docs.
[04:57] Samir: Perfect. We'll do that. Jenna, can you capture the tech deliverables?
[05:01] Jenna: Yep, I'll share the benchmark guide and a sample script. Also, can you tell us about your tokenization and stop sequences? Some parity issues come from tokenizer differences.
[05:12] Luca: We use GPT-2 tokenizer for most models but have a few edge cases with custom tokenizers; we can include that in the artifact bundle.
[05:19] Jenna: Great. Also note: when running quantized variants you'll sometimes see small numeric diffs; our monitoring flags those so you can accept/reject by eval metric thresholds.
[05:31] Maya: About on-prem vs VPC: compliance team prefers data not leave our VPC for certain PII flows. We may need Private or at least VPC-only flows.
[05:42] Samir: Understood. We have Private deployment options and on-prem packages for air-gapped environments. We'll include the options in the doc.
[05:51] Luca: Bench specifics: can we test batch embeddings throughput and chat latency with identical prompts?
[05:56] Jenna: Yes. Please send sample prompt set and a small dataset. We'll run side-by-side against OpenAI baseline and provide delta metrics.
[06:06] Maya: For success criteria: 1) per-token cost reduced by ~3x, 2) p95 chat latency <300ms, 3) quality no worse than -2% on our eval metrics.
[06:17] Samir: Good explicit criteria. We'll model the pilot against those.
[06:22] Jonas: Will you need network peering info early? We can prepare firewall rules.
[06:26] Jenna: If you choose Dedicated with VPC peering, yes we'll need network details during POC. For Private/on-prem there are different steps. We'll coordinate once pilot is greenlit.
[06:37] Maya: Any notes about model upgrades and rollouts? We can't have sudden regressions mid-quarter.
[06:42] Samir: We support pinned model versions and canary rollouts; we can also maintain legacy variants for a period.
[06:48] Priya: Also curious about observability — token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[06:53] Jenna: That's in Redwood Console; we'll provide sample screenshots. You get token-level breakdown, per-route latency, and error traces.
[07:01] Luca: One more technical: does Redwood support KV cache reuse across sessions for multi-turn state? We rely on that heavily.
[07:07] Jenna: Yes, KV cache is supported and the runtime manages it for continuous batching to lower per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs.
[07:16] Maya: Ok that answers most.
[07:18] Samir: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs, Jenna will share benchmark guide and runbook, Celestia to send sample prompts and tokenization artifacts, schedule a perf deep dive next week.
[07:32] Priya: Sounds good.
[07:34] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:35] Samir: Thanks. We'll follow up via email after the call.
[07:39] *call ends*

Notes: transcription had some minor mislabels, a few words unclear (e.g., tokenization spelled as tok-enization in one segment). Shared artifacts referenced: Redwood Dedicated deck (link: https://redwood.ai/deck), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/celestia-template), security pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack)
